claims.statement: IEA PVPS describes inverter failures as a major source of revenue loss and shows how historical failure analysis can identify component and environmental causes. An installer-led exchange can plausibly control the failed-unit intake, fault record, and replacement decision, but access to firmware, components, and qualified repair capacity is not proved.

The present measurable loss is generation revenue forgone while a failed inverter is diagnosed and replaced, plus the price of a new unit. IEA PVPS calls the inverter a major cause of lost revenue and cites high shares of reported troubles, though the report is older and Polish residential outage economics need current measurement.

The payer hypothesis is the installer or asset owner using O&M and replacement budget at equipment failure for a guaranteed-turnaround repair or tested exchange. IEA PVPS finds repair and reuse technically feasible but often labor-intensive and costly; EU right-to-repair rules show policy direction, but direct applicability to PV inverters is unconfirmed.

contrary_evidence: The 2026 IEA PVPS report warns that repair can remain labor-intensive, costly, and difficult to scale.
OEM warranties, locked firmware, unavailable components, and rapidly falling new-equipment prices can make independent repair uneconomic.

economics.acquisition_route: Collect 30-50 failed inverters or control boards from the family business and partner installers, classify faults before buying repair equipment, and contract an electronics lab for fixed-price repairs with a limited exchange warranty.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A regional reverse-logistics exchange could expand into multi-brand spare-parts inventory, repair routing, and predictive failure data for aging distributed-energy assets; the founder objective requires high repair yield and installer-network scale.
economics.founder_time: About 12-18 hours per week for triage data, partner management, and marketplace operations; certified technicians and repair labs handle electrical work.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Exchange price less repair-lab fee, shipping, failed-repair rate, test time, and warranty reserve; data subscription is possible only after enough installed-base history exists.
economics.payback: Require each repair batch to turn inventory within 60 days and recover acquisition, test, and warranty reserve before expanding model coverage.
economics.pricing: Fixed tested-exchange price below new replacement cost, refundable core deposit, and optional installer membership for priority turnaround.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Installers repeatedly encounter failures across their installed base; core returns and compatibility history reinforce the exchange.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Multi-brand fault taxonomy, repair-yield history, compatible spare inventory, and dense installer reverse logistics
fingerprint.customer: Regional PV and heat-pump installers plus owners of out-of-warranty distributed-energy assets
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Installer membership and core-return logistics initiated at field diagnosis
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Tested repair/exchange with core deposit and limited warranty, later augmented by failure intelligence
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Installer or owner pays when a failed inverter or control board stops an asset and replacement is authorized
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An out-of-warranty renewable-energy controller fails and a new OEM replacement is slow or expensive

founder_fit: The family company can provide authentic failure cases and installer distribution from day one.
Failure classification, parts forecasting, and repair-yield prediction use the founder's data skills.
Repair work and warranty testing can be outsourced, keeping founder effort focused on the system.
risks: Electrical safety and warranty liability can be severe if a refurbished unit fails.
A small and fragmented model inventory may tie up capital without finding matching demand.
Manufacturer parts, schematics, and firmware may remain inaccessible despite broader repair policy.

structure.commercial_archetype: Managed reverse-logistics exchange and repair network
structure.control_point: Installer-controlled failed-unit intake, diagnostic record, and core-return decision
structure.critical_dependency: Repeatable repair yield with safe testing, accessible parts, and warranty economics below new replacement

thesis: Backcast from an aging distributed-energy fleet where repairability and parts intelligence are strategic: capture failed hardware at the installer visit now, turn cores into guaranteed exchanges, and let fault and compatibility data compound faster than any local repair shop.
title: Renewable Repair Exchange
uncertainties: The current volume and model concentration of failed inverters and heat-pump boards in the reachable installer base are unknown.
Repair success, turnaround, and warranty-return distributions need a physical batch test.
Direct scope of EU repair rules for the target equipment requires legal verification.
